curriculum.lesson_evidence: Sharing a tradition means choosing what you want to share, preparing clear information about what it is and why it matters, and presenting respectfully. Use kind words about other people's traditions. Food can only be shared with school permission and attention to allergies.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

lesson.child_mission: Sharing a tradition means choosing what you want to share, preparing clear information about what it is and why it matters, and presenting respectfully. Use kind words about other people's traditions. Food can only be shared with school permission and attention to allergies.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Rewrite "That food is weird" as a respectful comment.

FEEDBACK
For example: "I have not tried that before. Can you tell me about it?"

WATCH FOR
Using words like weird or strange to describe a tradition is unkind and closes down learning.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Prepare a two-minute presentation or poster on a tradition you want to share. Include name, who takes part, why it matters, one question for the class and an allergy note. Practise using respectful words.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Sharing a tradition means choosing what you want to share, preparing clear information about what it is and why it matters, and presenting respectfully. Use kind words about other people's traditions. Food can only be shared with school permission and attention to allergies.
materials: Optional: local map, photo or interview notes
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.

Parent: Likely misconception: Using words like weird or strange to describe a tradition is unkind and closes down learning. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating share on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with share, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.
